text:
oncall-bot: PAGER ALERT — Dedicated pool 'resv-q3' at 99% GPU utilization, sustained queue growth (>5m). Multiple reserved tenants reporting increased latency and intermittent 503s. Assigned to aisha (oncall).

aisha: joining the thread. pulling dashboards and logs now. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre for immediate help.

ben: i see autoscaler flatlined at 12 replicas and hit max_replicas at 02:03 UTC. queue climbed from 30 -> 480 in ~18 minutes. top consumer is Enterprise:NovaHealth (long-lived sessions), second is AnalyticsBatch (lots of tiny parallel jobs).

carlos: packing looks poor — many sessions with large KV caches preventing consolidation. also a burst of small requests prevents efficient batching.

mike: CS reports from two enterprise customers about timeouts. NovaHealth says their scheduled analytics run started ~01:55 UTC and they can't change it mid-run.

aisha: immediate actions: (1) evict low-priority/background sessions to free slots, (2) enable emergency scale-up (temporary raise max_replicas), (3) apply model-fallback for best-effort endpoints to reduce GPU load. who can run evict?

ben: running eviction for background sessions now:

```
# evict background sessions from pool
python infra/evict.py --pool resv-q3 --priority background --limit 50
```

ben: eviction executed at 02:12 UTC — evicted 34 sessions. queue dropped slightly but still >200.

deploy-bot: recent deploy: eng-runtime/autoscaler v2.14 deployed 01:40 UTC. Change: default max_replicas lowered 20->12 to control spend. Rollout status: success.

carlos: that explains ceiling. request: increase max_replicas to 24 temporarily. need oncall approval.

aisha: approve emergency increase to 24 for this pool. ben, go ahead.

ben: patching autoscaler config now:

```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap autoscaler-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"resv-q3.max_replicas":"24"}}'
```

ben: change applied at 02:18 UTC. provisioning new GPUs, ETA ~5m.

carlos: while nodes spin up, we pushed routing override for non-critical enterprise routes to fallback llama-7b-quant. this cuts token CPU/GPU by ~40%.

ben: fallback pushed at 02:20 UTC. observed per-request token rate drop and immediate improvement in token throughput.

mike: notif to affected customers drafted. opened a customer bridge for NovaHealth; CSMs joined, they requested a post-incident writeup and SLA impact estimate.

ben: new nodes came up at 02:24 UTC; autoscaler at 21/24 replicas. queue shrank 210 -> 28 by 02:28 UTC.

oncall-bot: Incident status update: severity lowered P1 -> P2. Mitigation active.

carlos: follow-up items: (a) revert the cost-driven max_replicas default for pools with reserved enterprise tenants, (b) add a burst-credit override to permit short spikes above max without immediate throttling, (c) improve session packing heuristics to prefer consolidating KV-heavy sessions.

aisha: creating postmortem ticket and assigning eng-runtime + eng-sre. also adding alert threshold change: warn at 85% sustained for >3m instead of >5m.

mike: will include customer timeline and messages into postmortem and coordinate SLA calc with finance.

ben: saved timeline/log snippets for RC:

```
autoscaler.default_max=12
pool.resv-q3.util=99.1
top-tenants: NovaHealth 46%, AnalyticsBatch 27%, others 27%
```

aisha: final check 02:40 UTC: pool util 58%, queue 6, no new customer errors. leaving monitoring on for 30m. will hand off to next shift at 03:10 UTC with notes.

mike: posted interim update to NovaHealth CSM and ops. they'll wait for postmortem. thanks team. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident mitigated. Duration: 02:03 UTC - 02:28 UTC (active mitigation). Please add any residual notes to this thread before closing.
